seed-article-1.t: 5 Reasons Small Businesses Need Their Own Website
seed-article-1.e: Social media helps, but your own website gives your business an official address that is easy to find, trusted, and fully in your hands.
c: A desk with a laptop for managing a business website
Your own website makes your business easier to find and trust.
b: Many small businesses already sell through Instagram, WhatsApp, or marketplaces. That is a good start. But when potential customers search for your business on Google, what do they find? This is where your own website comes in.
1. Easy to find on Google

People looking for a product or service usually start with a search engine. A tidy website that uses the words customers search for gives your business a chance to show up, without paying for ads all the time.
2. Look more convincing
An official website tells people your business is serious and trustworthy. New customers who do not know you yet feel more comfortable getting in touch or placing an order.
A laptop, an iPad, and an iPhone side by side, all switched on
A website that looks tidy on phones and computers makes customers more confident.
3. All your information in one place
No more answering the same questions over and over. Just point customers to a website that includes:
A full list of products or services with photos
Prices and how to order
Opening hours, address, and a location map
A WhatsApp button that opens right away
4. Do not depend on a single platform
The rules and algorithms of social media or marketplaces can change at any time. A website is yours: its look, its content, and its customer data are all in your hands.
5. It can grow with your business
You do not need to build something big right away. Start with a simple website, then add features such as a full catalog, online ordering, or stock tracking as your business grows.
Start simple, then add features as your business grows.
Where to start?

seed-article-2.t: How to Choose the Right Website Development Service
seed-article-2.e: Not sure how to choose a website provider? Use this simple guide to compare, ask the right questions, and make sure the result fits your business needs.
c: A team discussing around a meeting table
Discussing your needs up front helps you pick the right provider.
b: There are many website development services to choose from, from freelancers to agencies. To avoid regrets halfway through, check the following before you decide.
1. Define the goal of your website first
What is the website for? Answer these questions:
Do you only need a neat business profile?
Do customers need to order or pay directly?
Is there data you want to manage, such as stock or registrations?
A clear goal makes the quotes you receive easier to compare.
2. Look at examples of their work

A good provider has a portfolio. Open their example websites on your phone and check whether they look tidy, load quickly, and are easy to understand. If possible, ask whether their clients are happy to be contacted.
A sketch of a website page layout on paper
A design reviewed together at the start prevents misunderstandings.
3. Ask what is included in the price
Two quotes with similar prices can contain very different things. Make sure you know whether the price includes:
A domain (the website address)
Hosting (where the website is stored)
Maintenance after the website goes live
Revisions and how many you get
4. Make sure there is a design approval step
You have the right to see and approve the design before development starts. Working this way reduces the risk of a final result far from what you imagined.
5. Check how it looks on a phone
Most visitors open websites on their phones. A website that looks great on a computer but messy on a phone will drive customers away.
6. Choose someone who is easy to communicate with
A website is a long-term collaboration. A provider who replies quickly, explains things in simple language, and is honest about time and cost is much more pleasant to work with.

seed-article-3.t: How Much Does a Website Cost? A Beginner's Guide
seed-article-3.e: Website prices can vary widely depending on your needs. Understand the cost components so you can compare quotes with more confidence.
c: A laptop showing charts and data
Website cost depends on your needs and the features you choose.
b: "So how much does it cost to build a website?" The honest answer is: it depends. To avoid confusion, first get to know what makes up the cost of a website.
What makes up the cost of a website?
**Design and development**: building the look, pages, and features
**Domain**: the website address, such as yourbusiness.com, usually paid yearly
**Hosting**: where the website is stored so it can be opened at any time
**Maintenance**: upkeep, small fixes, and updates after launch
**Extra features**: online payments, an order system, user login, and so on
Why do prices differ so much?
A one-page website for a business profile is naturally simpler than an online store with a shopping cart and reports. The more features and pages, the more work is needed.
An analytics dashboard on a laptop screen
Features such as dashboards and reports widen the scope of work.
A simple website or a complete system?

For a business that is just starting out, a profile website with a WhatsApp button is usually enough. A more complete system, such as stock tracking, online registration, or automation, makes sense once manual work starts piling up.

**Large Package**, from Rp 2 million per year: a multi-page website or app, an information and operations system, business process automation, user role settings, plus free maintenance and hosting for 1 year.

Tips to save money without sacrificing quality
Start with what matters most, then add features later.
Prepare your materials (logo, photos, text) before work begins so there are no extra costs from waiting.
Ask clearly what is already included in the price.

seed-article-4.t: What Is Business Automation? Simple Examples for Small Businesses
seed-article-4.e: Automation is not only for big companies. Discover simple examples that can save a small business time and reduce data entry mistakes.
c: A robot arm on an automated production line
Automation runs repetitive work on its own.
b: When they hear the word "automation", many people picture robots in a factory. In a small business, however, automation is often something far simpler: repetitive work that a system carries out on its own.
Automation is actually simple
The idea is this: if you do a task with the same steps every time, chances are it can be run automatically. You save time, and the risk of typing mistakes goes down.
Commonly used examples
A new order comes in, then a notification is sent straight to the owner's WhatsApp.
A daily sales report is created and sent automatically every night.
Customers receive payment reminders without anyone having to remind them manually.
Data from a website form goes into a spreadsheet automatically.
A worker monitoring a machine with a laptop
Automation reduces repetitive manual work.
When does your business need automation?
The signs usually make themselves felt:
A lot of time goes into moving data from one place to another.
There are often recording mistakes or missed orders.
You are always the "go-between" for different parts of the business.
Reports are only finished after hours of preparation.
Start with the one task that eats the most time
You do not need to automate everything at once. Pick the one task that wears you out the most, tidy up its flow, then automate it. Once you feel the benefit, move on to the next one.
Automate what repeats, so your time goes to what truly needs a human decision.
Have repetitive work you would like to streamline? Tell us, consultations are free anytime.

seed-article-5.e: Get these materials ready first so your website is built quickly and turns out the way you hoped. It is fine if they are not complete yet.
c: A hand writing a plan in a notebook
Preparing your materials first makes the website go faster.
b: Building a website goes much more smoothly when the materials are ready. Here is a simple list you can check off one by one.
1. Business identity
Business or brand name
Logo (if you have one), ideally as a clear image file
Colors you usually use on packaging or social media
2. Website content
A short story about your business and what makes it different
A list of products or services with prices
How to order or get in touch
Questions customers often ask
Sticky notes and a layout draft on a desk
Writing ideas down helps organize your website content.
3. Photos and visuals
Real photos of your products and premises are almost always more convincing than stock images. Prepare:
Product photos from several angles
Photos of your premises or your process
Team photos, if you want to show them
4. Contact and location
A WhatsApp number for orders
Full address and opening hours
Social media accounts you want to link
5. Design references
Collect a few websites you like, even from different industries. References help us understand your taste quickly.
If your materials are not complete, that is okay. We will help tidy them up and tell you which parts still need to be filled in.

seed-article-6.t: Why Website Speed Affects Your Sales
seed-article-6.e: Visitors are impatient. Understand why a fast website keeps potential customers around, and what you can do about it.
c: Performance charts and numbers on a screen
A website that opens fast keeps visitors around longer.
b: Imagine tapping a link and the page just does not show up. How long are you willing to wait? Most people give up within seconds, and your potential customers are no different.
A slow website drives customers away

Visitors who arrive from Google or social media are usually comparing several options. If your website is slow, they simply close it and open a competitor's. The sale is lost before you even get to explain anything.
Why websites feel slow
Very large photos that were never made smaller
Too many widgets, animations, or third-party scripts
Weak hosting, or hosting too far from your visitors
Code that was not kept tidy from the start
A laptop lit up in a dark room
A lightweight website feels instant, even on a mobile network.
Simple steps to a faster website
Reduce the size of photos and use a modern format such as WebP.
Show only what is really needed on the home page.
Choose reliable hosting with a content delivery network (CDN).
Test your website regularly with PageSpeed Insights.
At Nocoding, websites are built with optimized images and lightweight code from the start, so they stay comfortable to open on a phone with an ordinary signal.
A fast website is not a luxury. It is part of serving your customers.

seed-article-7.t: Basic SEO for Local Businesses: How to Show Up on Google
seed-article-7.e: You do not need to be an expert. A few basic steps make your business easier to find for people nearby who are searching.
c: A laptop and phone showing search results
Basic SEO helps your business appear when customers search.
b: Every day, people type "cake shop near me" or "AC repair in Yogyakarta" into Google. If your business does not show up, that customer goes elsewhere. Basic SEO helps you answer searches like these.
What is SEO?

SEO (Search Engine Optimization) is the practice of tidying up a website so search engines can understand it easily. As a result, your website has a chance to rank higher when people search for what you offer.
Basic steps you can start today
**Write with the words customers use.** Use everyday language, not technical terms.
**Mention your location.** Name the city or service area on your home page.
**Complete your Google Business profile.** Fill in the address, opening hours, photos, and phone number.
**Write clear page titles.** One page, one topic.
**Make sure your website works well on a phone.** Search engines prioritize the mobile view.
A phone screen full of different apps
Most local searches are done on a phone.
Consistency matters more than tricks

Your business name, address, and phone number should be exactly the same on your website, Google Business profile, and social media. Consistent information gives search engines more confidence and gives customers more trust.
Add articles regularly
Writing articles about questions customers often ask helps your website show up for more searches. Starting with one article a month is enough.

seed-article-8.t: Website or App? Which One Fits Your Business
seed-article-8.e: Both are useful, but they serve different needs. Learn the difference so you do not spend money on something you do not need yet.
c: A laptop showing program code
Choose a solution based on your business needs, not on trends.
b: "Should I build a website or an app?" This question comes up often. The answer depends on what you want to achieve, not on which one sounds cooler.
When is a website enough?
A website fits when your goal is to introduce your business, show your products or services, and make it easy for customers to reach you. Anyone can open it in a browser, with nothing to download.
A business profile and product catalog
Ordering through WhatsApp or a form
Articles and information that bring in visitors from Google
When is an app or system a better fit?
An app or information system is useful when there are processes to manage, for example data entered by many people or work organized by role.
Stock and daily transaction records
Online registration or queues
Automatic reports and access control for your team
A monitor displaying a design system interface
A good system is designed around how the business actually works.
You do not have to choose just one
Many businesses start with a simple website, then add a system once manual work starts piling up. This keeps costs light and lets development follow real needs.

seed-article-9.t: Simple Steps to Keep Your Business Website Secure
seed-article-9.e: Even a small website can be a target. Apply these basic habits to protect your business data and your customers' trust.
c: Glowing electronics on a circuit board
Website security starts with consistent basic habits.
b: Many business owners assume a small website is of no interest to hackers. In reality, attacks often run automatically and look for weaknesses in any website. The good news is that basic steps already help a lot.
1. Use strong, different passwords
Avoid birthdays or your business name. Use long, unique passwords for every service, and keep them in a password manager so you do not have to memorize them.
2. Make sure your website uses HTTPS
The padlock in the website address shows that visitor data is sent encrypted. It also makes customers trust you more, and search engines like it too.
Program code on a laptop screen
Regular updates and maintenance close security gaps.
3. Update and maintain it regularly
Security holes are usually found in software that has not been updated for a long time. That is why regular maintenance is not just an extra; it is part of keeping your website safe.
4. Limit who has access
Give access only to people who really need it.
Remove access for team members who are no longer involved.
Never share passwords in group chats.
5. Keep backups
A backup lets you restore your website quickly if something goes wrong. Make sure your website provider does this regularly.
Nocoding packages already include 1 year of maintenance, so basic upkeep is not something you have to think about yourself.

seed-article-10.t: How to Build a Small Business Website in 5 Steps
seed-article-10.e: Never built a website before? Follow these five simple steps, from setting your goal to a website ready to share with customers.
c: A man using a laptop while enjoying a coffee
A good website starts with a clear goal.
b: Building a website sounds complicated, but the process can be broken into a few small steps. With the right order, you do not need to know programming to have a tidy website that is ready for selling.
1. Set the goal of your website
Ask yourself: what is this website for? Introducing your business, showing a catalog, or taking orders? One main goal makes every later decision easier.
2. Gather your materials
Prepare what you will show:
Business name and logo
Photos of your products or premises
A list of products or services with prices
WhatsApp number and address
A sketch of a website page layout on paper
A simple sketch helps decide how the pages are arranged.
3. Choose your website name and address
Pick a domain name that is short, easy to remember, and easy to type, for example based on your business name. Avoid hyphens and confusing numbers.
4. Decide how to build it
You can build it yourself, or ask a service provider for help. If your time is limited, handing it to a provider gives a tidier result and a faster launch.
5. Test, then share

Before announcing it, open the website on a phone and a computer. Make sure the text is readable, the WhatsApp button works, and the photos look clear. Then share the address on social media, packaging, and business cards.

seed-article-11.t: Landing Page or Company Profile: Which Fits Your Business?
seed-article-11.e: These two types of websites are often mixed up. Learn how their purposes differ so you can choose the one that suits your goals.
c: A computer screen showing a web page
A landing page guides visitors toward a single action.
b: When ordering a website you may hear two terms: landing page and company profile. Both are websites, but they do different jobs.
What is a landing page?
A landing page is a single page focused on one goal, such as getting visitors to order, sign up, or contact you on WhatsApp. Its content is short and straight to the point.
Good for promoting a specific product or event.
Good for new businesses with a limited budget.
Easy to read because there is only one flow.
What is a company profile?
A company profile is a website that introduces your business in full. It usually has several pages, such as about us, services, portfolio, and contact.
Good for businesses that want to look credible in front of clients.
Good when your services need a more detailed explanation.
Contains more keywords, so it is easier to find on Google.
A laptop displaying a collection of images and designs
A company profile gives room to show your portfolio.
Which one should you choose?

If your goal is simple and quick, start with a landing page. If you want to build a name and trust for the long term, a company profile is a better fit. You can also combine them: a landing page for promotions, and a company profile as the main home of your business.

A good domain is easy to type without mistakes.

A stable address helps your website's reputation in the eyes of search engines over time.
Tips for choosing a domain name

Keep it short and easy to spell.
Avoid numbers and hyphens.
Choose a common extension, such as .com or .id.

seed-article-13.t: Why Phone Display Decides Customers' First Impression
seed-article-13.e: Most visitors open websites on their phones. A messy display on a small screen can make them leave right away.
c: A phone and laptop showing social media
Customers often open a website for the first time on their phone.
b: When they see a link on social media or in search results, most people open it on their phone. If the layout is cramped, the text is tiny, or the buttons are hard to tap, they will not stay long.
What is a responsive website?
A responsive website adapts its layout to the screen size. On a phone, columns stack downward. On a computer, columns can sit side by side. The content is the same; only the layout changes.
Signs of a website that is comfortable on a phone
Text is large enough without pinching to zoom.
Buttons are easy to press with a thumb.
Photos are not cropped and not too heavy.
The menu is compact and easy to open.
Nothing has to be scrolled sideways.
A tablet showing an online store among plants
A tidy layout makes shopping on a phone feel easy.
How to check
Open your website on your own phone.
Try it on another phone with a different screen size.
Tap all the important buttons, especially the WhatsApp button.
Notice how fast the website loads on mobile data.

seed-article-14.t: How to Use a WhatsApp Button on Your Website to Get More Orders
seed-article-14.e: Customers prefer to ask questions through the app they already use every day. Here is how to place a WhatsApp button the right way.
c: A notebook, phone, and glasses on a white desk
One tap connects customers straight to you.
b: In Indonesia, WhatsApp is the most natural way for customers to ask questions and place orders. That is why an easy-to-find WhatsApp button is often more effective than a long form.
1. Put it where it is easy to see
Place the button at the top of the page and at the end of every product description. A floating button in the corner of the screen also helps, as long as it does not cover the content.
2. Prepare a clear starting message
The button can send a ready-made message, for example "Hello, I would like to order a birthday cake". A starting message saves customers time and lets you know right away what they need.
3. Use a specific call to action
Wording like "Order Now" or "Ask for a Price" is clearer than just "Contact Us".
A hand holding a phone showing a payment terminal
A clear starting message speeds up the ordering process.
4. Reply quickly
A button is only useful if messages get answered. Set clear reply hours, and prepare answers to the questions that come up most often.
Websites built by Nocoding come with a WhatsApp button whose starting message can be customized.

seed-article-15.t: Your Own Online Store or a Marketplace? Here Is the Comparison
seed-article-15.e: Marketplaces have plenty of buyers, while your own store gives you full control. Understand the strengths of each before you decide.
c: A hand holding a credit card in front of a laptop
Choose where to sell based on your goals and your business's capacity.
b: Many sellers start on a marketplace because it is practical. As the business grows, a question appears: should you have your own online store? The answer is not either-or.
Strengths of marketplaces
Buyers are plentiful from day one.
Payment and shipping systems are already in place.
Quick to start without having to build anything.
Limits of marketplaces
Rules, fees, and appearance are set by the platform.
Customers are considered the platform's, not yours.
Your store competes directly with other stores on the same page.
Strengths of your own online store
You control the look and the shopping experience.
Customer data stays in your hands.
Your brand feels stronger and is easier to remember.
A cashier tablet on a wooden table
Your own store gives you full control over sales.
A strategy that often works
Use marketplaces to reach new buyers, then guide loyal customers to your website or WhatsApp for their next orders. That way you stay busy while also building an asset of your own.

seed-article-16.e: Not every business needs a shopping cart. A simple online catalog is enough to showcase products and take orders through WhatsApp.
c: A shop owner serving a customer with a cashier tablet
A clear catalog makes it easy for customers to choose.
b: An online catalog is a page that shows your products or services complete with photos, descriptions, and prices. Customers can browse any time, then order through WhatsApp.
What should a catalog include?
Clear product photos from several sides.
A name and a short description.
A price or a price range.
An order button that connects directly to WhatsApp.

Group products by category so they are easy to find.
Write descriptions that answer common questions, such as size, material, or flavor.
Put your best sellers at the top.
Update prices and availability regularly.

seed-article-17.t: Google Business Profile for Local Businesses: A Step-by-Step Guide
seed-article-17.e: A Google profile helps customers find your location, opening hours, and contact straight from search results and maps.
c: A barista preparing an order with a tablet in a cafe
A complete Google profile helps local businesses get found.
b: When people search for "coffee near me" or "nearest motorbike repair shop", Google shows a map and a list of businesses. Businesses with a complete profile have a better chance of showing up and being chosen.

Google Business Profile is a free profile that shows your business name, address, opening hours, phone number, photos, and customer reviews on Google Search and Google Maps.

Keeping your profile alive

seed-article-18.t: How to Write Website Text That Is Easy to Understand and Sells
seed-article-18.e: Clear text lets visitors quickly understand what you offer. Apply these five simple principles when you write.
c: A hand writing on paper near a laptop
Clear text is more convincing than complicated words.
b: A great design is useless if visitors do not understand what you offer. Writing website text is not as hard as it seems, as long as you follow a few principles.
1. Start from the customer's needs
Write from the customer's point of view. Instead of "We provide catering services", try "Your event runs smoothly without worrying about food".
2. Use everyday language
Avoid complicated terms. If you must use a technical term, explain it briefly.
3. One paragraph, one idea
Short paragraphs are more comfortable to read on a phone screen. Break long text into small sections with clear headings.
A fountain pen writing on paper
Concise writing makes your message easier to remember.
4. Show benefits, not just features
Features explain what you have; benefits explain what the customer gains. Customers buy benefits.
5. End with a clear call to action
Every page should close with a next step, such as a "Order on WhatsApp" button. Do not leave visitors unsure of what to do.

seed-article-19.t: Product Photo Tips for Your Business Website
seed-article-19.e: Good photos make products look more convincing. You do not need an expensive camera, just a phone and a few good habits.
c: A desk with a notebook and printed photos
Neatly arranged photos make a product more appealing.
b: Online customers cannot touch your products, so they judge by the photos. Clear, consistent photos are often the difference between a quick glance and an order.
Simple preparation
Clean the product and the background.
Use a plain background, such as a white table or cloth.
Use natural light from near a window and avoid direct flash.
Tips for shooting with a phone
Clean the camera lens before shooting.
Take photos from several angles: front, side, and close-up details.
Keep the phone steady; lean it on something or use a small tripod if needed.
Keep the style, colors, and background consistent across all products.
A laptop and a cup of coffee on a wooden table
A simple background keeps the product in the spotlight.
Before uploading

Original phone photos are usually large. Reduce their size so your website stays fast to open, but not so much that the images turn blurry. Nocoding helps optimize images so they stay sharp yet light.

seed-article-20.t: Choosing Colors and Fonts So Your Website Looks Consistent
seed-article-20.e: Consistent colors and fonts make a website look tidy and memorable. Here is a simple guide for choosing them.
c: Three-dimensional icons of various apps
A consistent visual identity makes a brand easy to recognize.
b: A website that is pleasant to look at usually uses colors and fonts with discipline. You do not need to be a designer, just follow a few basic rules.
1. Pick one main color
Take it from your logo or product. The main color is used on buttons and on the parts you want to highlight.
2. Add one or two supporting colors
Supporting colors are used sparingly for backgrounds or accents. Too many colors make the look busy and confusing.
3. Make sure the text is easy to read
The contrast between text color and background is very important. Light gray text on a white background is hard to read, especially in bright sunlight.
A hand planning a design with a pencil near a laptop
A design planned from the start gives a tidy look.
4. Limit the number of fonts
Two typefaces are enough: one for headings and one for body text. Choose fonts that are clear and comfortable to read on small screens.
5. Apply them everywhere
Use the same colors and fonts on your website, social media, packaging, and printed materials. Consistency makes a brand easier to remember.

seed-article-21.t: User Experience: 7 Habits That Make a Website Easy to Use
seed-article-21.e: A website that is easy to use keeps visitors around and makes them more likely to contact you. Apply these seven simple habits.
c: Hands in discussion in front of a laptop showing a design
Talking with users helps find what confuses them.
b: User experience (UX) is how easy and comfortable it is for someone to use your website. A confusing website makes visitors leave, however beautiful it looks.
**Keep the menu short.** Show only the pages that really matter.
**Put the main information at the top.** Visitors should know what your business is within a few seconds.
**One page, one goal.** Avoid piling too many calls to action at once.
**Use clear buttons.** The label says what happens when it is pressed.
**Keep forms short.** Ask only for the data you really need.
**Leave some empty space.** A roomy layout is easier to read.
**Test it with other people.** Ask a friend to open the website and see which parts confuse them.
A team smiling while looking at a laptop screen together
Feedback from others often finds what we overlooked.
Start small
You do not have to change everything at once. Pick one habit, apply it, and see the result. Small, consistent improvements make a website more comfortable over time.

seed-article-23.t: Automatic Sales Reports: Save Time and Avoid Recording Mistakes
seed-article-23.e: Preparing sales reports by hand takes time. Automation lets daily or weekly reports assemble and send themselves.

Data is scattered across notebooks, chats, and spreadsheets.
A mistyped number is hard to notice.
The report is only done after hours of work.
Decisions are delayed because the data is not ready.

Sales data is collected from one source, then calculated and summarized on a schedule. The result can be sent to WhatsApp or email, or shown on a dashboard that you can open any time.

Total sales per day, week, and month.

A comparison with the previous period.
Notes on stock that is running low.

seed-article-24.t: When Does Your Business Need a Stock Tracking System?
seed-article-24.e: Stock kept in a notebook or spreadsheet becomes a hassle as goods multiply. Learn the signs that a stock system is needed.
c: A card transaction at a payment machine
Every transaction changes how much stock is available.
b: At first, keeping stock in a notebook is enough. But as the number of goods and transactions grows, manual records become hard to follow.
Signs you need a stock system
The stock in your records often differs from the stock in the warehouse or on the shelf.
Items run out without anyone noticing, so orders get turned down.
Goods pile up because nobody knows which ones sell slowly.
More than one person keeps the records and the data does not match.
Documents, a phone, and a calculator on a desk
Scattered records make stock hard to monitor.
Benefits of a stock tracking system
The number of goods is updated every time there is a sale.
Automatic alerts when stock runs low.
Reports on best sellers and slow-moving items.
Different access levels for the owner and staff.
How to get started?
Start by listing all your goods and their starting quantities. Then decide who may record goods coming in and going out. A good system is designed around how you work, not the other way around.

seed-article-26.t: Reading Website Visitor Data: A Basic Guide for Beginners
seed-article-26.e: Visitor data shows what works and what needs fixing. Get to know the basic numbers worth keeping an eye on.
c: A laptop showing an analytics dashboard
An analytics dashboard summarizes how visitors behave on your website.
b: Once your website is live, the next question is: is anyone visiting it? Where do they come from, and which pages do they open most? Analytics tools such as Google Analytics help answer these questions.
Basic numbers worth understanding
**Visitors:** how many people opened the website in a given period.
**Sources:** where they came from, such as Google, social media, or typing the address directly.
**Popular pages:** the pages opened most often.
**Devices:** whether visitors use a phone or a computer.
**Visit times:** the hours or days when the website is busiest.
A laptop screen showing program code
Tracking that is set up correctly produces data you can trust.
How to use the data
If most visitors use a phone, make sure the mobile display is truly comfortable.
If one page is opened the most, add a call to action on that page.
If many visitors come from social media, prepare content that matches that source.
Do not get trapped by numbers

Data is a clue, not the goal. Focus on what affects your business, such as the number of WhatsApp messages coming in. Nocoding can install analytics tools such as Google Analytics so you can understand visitor behavior.

seed-article-27.t: Social Media and Your Website: Complementing Each Other, Not Competing
seed-article-27.e: Social media is great for reaching new people, while a website is your business's official home. Use both with the right roles.
c: A phone showing social media app icons
Social media reaches new people, your website holds on to them.
b: A common question: if I am already active on Instagram or TikTok, do I still need a website? The answer is yes, because they play different roles.
The role of social media
Reaching new people through engaging content.
Building closeness with customers.
Spreading promos and news quickly.
The role of a website
Serving as an official address with complete, organized information.
Being easy to find through Google search.
Not depending on the rules and algorithms of any one platform.
A pink Instagram logo
A single link in your profile can send followers to your website.
How to combine them
Put your website address in the profile of every social media account.
Use social media to catch attention, then point people to your website for full information.
Show your social media links on your website so visitors can follow you.
Use the same photos and colors so your brand feels consistent.
This way, every follower has a chance to become a customer who knows your business more deeply.

seed-article-28.t: How to Build Customer Trust on Your Website
seed-article-28.e: New customers need a reason to trust you. A few simple elements on your website help your business look dependable.
c: Two people shaking hands
Trust is built on honesty and consistency.
b: When shopping online, customers cannot meet you face to face. That is why your website needs to give signs that your business is real and deserves trust.
1. Show a clear identity
Include your business name, address, WhatsApp number, and service hours. Open information shows you are not hiding anything.
2. Show your work and experience
Show photos of finished work, the making process, or examples of projects you have done. Real proof is more convincing than claims.
3. Collect genuine testimonials
Ask customers for permission to share their experience, then display it with their consent. Testimonials must truly come from customers. Made-up testimonials damage trust and can cause problems.
Two people high-fiving in front of a laptop

4. Explain prices and process
Transparent prices and a clear ordering flow reduce doubt. Customers do not like surprises at the end.
5. Keep your website well maintained
A website that is slow, broken, or out of date gives the impression of a business that is not looked after. Regular maintenance helps protect your reputation.

seed-article-30.t: Routine Website Maintenance: What Needs to Be Looked After?
seed-article-30.e: A website that is live still needs care to stay fast, secure, and accurate. Here is a list of things worth checking regularly.
c: A monitor showing React code
Routine maintenance keeps a website healthy.
b: Many people think a website is finished the moment it goes live. In fact, like a physical shop, a website needs care to stay pleasant to visit and trustworthy.
What to check regularly
**Business information.** Make sure the address, opening hours, prices, and contact numbers are still correct.
**Speed.** Check whether the website is still fast to open, especially after adding photos.
**Links and forms.** Try all the buttons, links, and the contact form.
**Security.** Update software and review access rights.
**Backups.** Make sure there is a copy that can be restored if something goes wrong.
**Domain and hosting expiry.** Do not let them lapse without noticing.
Python program code on a screen
Small, regular updates prevent big problems.
How often?
A light check once a month is enough. Security updates and data backups should run more regularly and automatically.
